paragraphs.title: Solomon’s Consolidation and Journey to Gibeon

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says that Solomon was strengthened in his kingdom.
easy.q: Who was strengthened in his kingdom?

easy.explanation: Solomon spoke to the captains, judges, governors, and chief fathers of Israel.
Solomon and all the congregation went to the high place at Gibeon.
easy.q: Where did Solomon and the congregation go?

answers: The tabernacle and the brasen altar were there
medium.explanation: The tabernacle of the congregation and the brasen altar were at Gibeon.
medium.q: Why did Solomon go to Gibeon?

answers: The worship tent where the congregation met before God
medium.explanation: The tabernacle was the sacred tent associated with the worship of God.
medium.q: What does the phrase “tabernacle of the congregation” refer to in this passage?

medium.explanation: Verse 6 says that Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings upon the altar.
medium.q: What did Solomon offer upon the brasen altar?

answers: His royal leadership was connected with worship of God
challenge.explanation: The gathering of Israel with Solomon at the sanctuary connects his leadership with worship.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Solomon going to Gibeon with the whole congregation?

answers: The ark was at Jerusalem, while the tabernacle was at Gibeon
challenge.explanation: David had brought the ark to Jerusalem, while the tabernacle and altar were at Gibeon.
challenge.q: What distinction does the passage make between the ark’s location and the tabernacle’s location?

challenge.explanation: The brasen altar had been made by Bezaleel, the son of Uri and grandson of Hur.
challenge.q: Why is Bezaleel mentioned in this passage?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says that God appeared to Solomon.
easy.q: Who appeared to Solomon in the night?

easy.explanation: Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge so that he could lead and judge the people.
easy.q: What did Solomon ask God to give him?

easy.explanation: Solomon came from Gibeon to Jerusalem and reigned over Israel.
easy.q: Where did Solomon go after his journey to Gibeon?

answers: To judge the great people of Israel
medium.explanation: He asked for wisdom and knowledge so he could judge God’s great people.
medium.q: Why did Solomon ask for wisdom and knowledge?

answers: A request for wisdom and knowledge
A request for the death of his enemies
medium.explanation: God was pleased that Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge instead of riches or long life.

answers: A foreign army and new territory
medium.explanation: God promised Solomon riches, wealth, and honour as well.
medium.q: What did God give Solomon in addition to wisdom and knowledge?

answers: He viewed it as a responsibility to judge the people
He viewed it mainly as a chance for trade
He viewed it as a reason to leave Israel
challenge.explanation: Solomon requested wisdom so he could lead and judge the people properly.
challenge.q: What does Solomon’s request reveal about how he viewed his role as king?

answers: To recall God’s mercy and his succession to David
challenge.explanation: Solomon acknowledged God’s great mercy to David and that he had been made king in David’s place.
challenge.q: Why did Solomon mention David his father in his prayer?

answers: Because Solomon asked for wisdom, he also received riches and honour
Because Solomon asked for riches, he received wisdom
Because Solomon built a palace, he became king
challenge.explanation: Since Solomon asked for wisdom rather than selfish gifts, God added riches, wealth, and honour.
challenge.q: What cause-and-effect relationship appears in God’s words to Solomon?

easy.explanation: Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen as part of his kingdom’s strength.
easy.q: How did Solomon strengthen his kingdom?

easy.explanation: Verse 14 records that Solomon had one thousand four hundred chariots.
easy.q: How many chariots did Solomon have?

easy.explanation: Solomon had horses brought out of Egypt.
easy.q: From which country were Solomon’s horses brought?

answers: He placed them in the chariot cities
He sent them to the tabernacle
He offered them on the altar
medium.explanation: He placed the chariots in the chariot cities, while some horsemen were with the king at Jerusalem.
medium.q: What did Solomon do with some of his chariots and horsemen?

answers: The silver was found only at Gibeon
medium.explanation: Silver and gold were made as plentiful in Jerusalem as stones.
medium.q: What does the description of silver and gold in Jerusalem show?

answers: Only to the people of Israel
To the kings of the Hittites and Syria
medium.explanation: The merchants brought them out for the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Syria.
medium.q: To whom did the king’s merchants bring horses and chariots?

answers: The horses and chariots supported the army and royal power
They were used to build the tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The chariots and horsemen are presented as important parts of Solomon’s military strength.
challenge.q: What was the connection between importing horses from Egypt and the strength of the kingdom?

answers: Solomon had commercial connections with other kingdoms
Egypt purchased all of Solomon’s horses
challenge.explanation: Trade with the Hittite and Syrian kings shows that Solomon’s kingdom had international commercial connections.
challenge.q: What can be learned from Solomon’s merchants selling to foreign kings?

answers: One thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen
Six hundred silver pieces and one hundred fifty horses
One thousand offerings and twelve governors
challenge.explanation: The passage gives one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen.
challenge.q: Which pair of numbers describes Solomon’s military strength?

easy.explanation: Verse 18 says that Solomon determined to build a house for the name of the Lord.
easy.q: What did Solomon determine to build for the Lord’s name?

easy.explanation: Solomon also determined to build a house for his kingdom.
easy.q: What else did Solomon determine to build?

easy.explanation: The first house was to be built for the name of the Lord.
easy.q: For whom was the first house intended?

answers: A house for the Lord’s name and a house for his kingdom
The tabernacle and the chariot cities
A horse storehouse and a marketplace
medium.explanation: The verse mentions a house for the Lord’s name and a house for Solomon’s kingdom.
medium.q: Which two buildings were included in Solomon’s plan?

answers: It expresses both his religious and royal establishment
It shows that he left Jerusalem
It was intended only for horse trading
medium.explanation: The plan includes both a house for the Lord and a royal house, showing religious and political establishment.
medium.q: How does the building plan relate to Solomon’s consolidation as king?

answers: The people who came from Egypt
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to Solomon’s royal authority and kingdom.
medium.q: What does “his kingdom” mean in the phrase “a house for his kingdom”?

answers: Solomon intended to establish both worship and royal government
Solomon wanted to abolish worship of God
Solomon planned only to build horse storehouses
challenge.explanation: The two houses represent the religious and royal centers of Solomon’s rule.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from planning a house for the Lord’s name alongside a house for his kingdom?

answers: He becomes established, receives wisdom and abundance, and then plans the buildings
He leaves the kingdom, travels to Egypt, and builds a tent
He sells horses, stops worship, and abolishes the monarchy
challenge.explanation: The chapter moves from Solomon’s establishment to God’s gifts and prosperity, then to his building plan.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas leads to Solomon’s building plan?

answers: One was for the Lord’s name and the other was for his kingdom
One was for horses and the other for trade
One was in Egypt and the other in Syria
challenge.explanation: The verse distinguishes between the house for the Lord’s name and the house for Solomon’s kingdom.
challenge.q: What is the main difference between the two houses in Solomon’s plan?
